description: Ex-RAAF/Army air observation post Auster. Struck off the civil register 05/07/2001 and retained on static display inside the museum hangar. Previously civil registered VH-CYH. Identity and current holder confirmed on ADF-Serials.
aliases: Auster Mk 3; Auster III; VH-CYH; VHCYH

description: Former British Army Air Corps airframe, never in Australian service; gifted to the Australian Army in 1970 and preserved at Oakey since. Identity and current holder confirmed on ADF-Serials.
Ex-Australian Army; crashed 26/06/1966, then a training aid at Wagga before going to the museum. Identity and current holder confirmed on ADF-Serials.
Served with 161 Recce Flight in Vietnam 1968-69; to the museum from storage in 1975. Identity and current holder confirmed on ADF-Serials.
Served with 161 Recce Flight in Vietnam; crashed in Papua New Guinea 10/1973 and restored by Brisbane TAFE before going to the museum. Identity and current holder confirmed on ADF-Serials.
Vietnam, Sinai and Bougainville veteran. Repainted overall red in the Operation Bel Isi scheme in 03/2014 and returned to display at the museum. Identity and current holder confirmed on ADF-Serials.
The first Australian Army Kiowa, handed over at Brisbane Airport 22/11/1971. Noted on display at the museum 02/2017. Identity and current holder confirmed on ADF-Serials.

Written off in an accident in the early 1990s and used as a RAEME training aid at Oakey. An airframe marked 44 is displayed at Oakey as the Kiowa Garden Display; ADF-Serials questions whether it is in fact A17-044.
Delivered 08/1956 and served with 1 Basic Flying Training School. Identity and current holder confirmed on ADF-Serials.
Served with 161 Recce Flight in Vietnam 1965-71 and flew the last Australian Army Cessna 180 sortie there on 14/02/1971. Identity and current holder confirmed on ADF-Serials.
Damaged at Laverton in 1966 and converted to a training aid; allotted to the museum for restoration to static display. Identity and current holder confirmed on ADF-Serials.

Delivered to 1st Aviation Regiment at Amberley 16/02/1968 after a 16-day ferry flight from Stans, Switzerland; served in Papua New Guinea. Registered VH-OWB to the museum 1994, withdrawn from the register 09/1998 and on static display. Identity and current holder confirmed on ADF-Serials.

Served with INTERFET in East Timor and Operation ANODE in the Solomon Islands. The museum was the successful tenderer in the 2015-16 disposal of six Caribou stored at Oakey. Identity and current holder confirmed on ADF-Serials.
Ex 5th Aviation Regiment, named Crux Australis and carrying the nose art Dusty Blonde. Retired to the museum. Identity and current holder confirmed on ADF-Serials.
First flew 06/09/1977 and was accepted by the RAAF 18/10/1977; flown to Oakey 19/10/1977. Placed on display at the museum 10/03/2004. Identity and current holder confirmed on ADF-Serials.
